name: Idiopathic hypersomnia
summary: Idiopathic hypersomnia is a central disorder of hypersomnolence with excessive daytime sleepiness, often long, unrefreshing sleep, and severe sleep inertia, without cataplexy. Low-sodium oxybate (Xywav) is the only FDA-approved treatment. Modafinil, methylphenidate, pitolisant, sodium oxybate, and clarithromycin are used off-label per AASM 2021. FDA refused to file pitolisant's IH sNDA (February 2025), and once-nightly sodium oxybate (Lumryz) had a positive phase 3 trial in 2026 but is not approved for IH.
plainSummary: Idiopathic hypersomnia causes heavy sleepiness during the day even after a long night's sleep, and it can be very hard to wake up. One medicine is FDA-approved for it, and doctors sometimes use others.

approved.generic: calcium, magnesium, potassium, and sodium oxybates (low-sodium oxybate)
approved.indication: Treatment of idiopathic hypersomnia (IH) in adults.

dosing.start: Twice nightly: 4.5 g/night or less, divided. Once nightly: 3 g or less
dosing.target: Individualized; titrate by up to 1.5 g/night per week
dosing.notes: Take at least 2 hours after eating, in bed. Doses may be divided equally or unequally. Hepatic impairment: start at half dose. Switch from Xyrem gram for gram.

boxedWarnings: CNS depression, including respiratory depression and obtundation
Abuse and misuse (GHB); available only through a restricted REMS program
approved.plainSummary: Xywav is a low-salt liquid medicine taken at night that helps adults with idiopathic hypersomnia feel less sleepy during the day. It is strictly controlled because it can slow breathing.

verified.note: Section 1.2 and the IH dosing (section 2.3) were checked on the Jazz SPL (effective July 2025). Approval year (2021) is from FDA approval history.

offLabel.notes: AASM 2021 gives a strong recommendation for adults with IH. Cautions: headache, anxiety, insomnia, rare serious rash, and reduced hormonal contraceptive efficacy.

details.labeledFor: FDA-approved for sleepiness in narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea, and shift work disorder; not for idiopathic hypersomnia.

dosing.target: 200–400 mg/day as one or two doses (second dose by early afternoon)
dosing.notes: Reduces the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives for up to a month after stopping.

warnings: Rare serious rash (SJS/TEN, DRESS) and angioedema
details.plainSummary: A wake-promoting medicine that is a first-line choice for sleepiness in idiopathic hypersomnia. It can cause headaches and weakens birth-control pills.

references.label: Maski K et al. AASM guideline: treatment of central disorders of hypersomnolence. J Clin Sleep Med 2021

offLabel.notes: Conditional AASM 2021 recommendation for adults. Cautions: misuse potential (C-II, boxed warning), elevated blood pressure and heart rate, insomnia, anxiety, and appetite loss.

details.labeledFor: FDA-approved for ADHD and narcolepsy; not for idiopathic hypersomnia.
formulations: ER tablets 10, 20 mg (Metadate ER, Methylin ER)
warnings: Increased blood pressure and heart rate
details.plainSummary: A stimulant used when other wake-promoting medicines are not enough. It can raise blood pressure and has misuse potential.

references.label: Maski K et al. AASM guideline: treatment of central disorders of hypersomnolence. J Clin Sleep Med 2021

offLabel.notes: Conditional AASM 2021 recommendation. The phase 3 INTUNE study missed its primary endpoint, and FDA issued a refusal-to-file letter for the IH sNDA in February 2025. Cautions: insomnia, headache, QT prolongation, CYP2D6/CYP3A4 interactions, and reduced hormonal contraceptive efficacy.

details.labeledFor: FDA-approved for sleepiness and cataplexy in narcolepsy (ages 6+); the FDA refused to file the IH application (Feb 2025).

dosing.start: 8.9 mg each morning for one week
dosing.notes: Halve the dose with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors; reduce in renal or hepatic impairment.

details.plainSummary: A non-stimulant wake-promoting medicine approved for narcolepsy that is sometimes used for idiopathic hypersomnia.

references.label: Maski K et al. AASM guideline: treatment of central disorders of hypersomnolence. J Clin Sleep Med 2021
NeurologyLive: FDA refuses to file Harmony sNDA for pitolisant in idiopathic hypersomnia (2025)

offLabel.agent: Sodium oxybate (Xyrem, generics, or once-nightly Lumryz)
offLabel.use: IH symptoms, including sleepiness and sleep inertia
offLabel.notes: Conditional AASM 2021 recommendation. Lumryz met its primary endpoint in the phase 3 REVITALYZ IH trial (May 2026), with an sNDA planned by end of 2026, but it is not FDA-approved for IH. Cautions: REMS restriction, respiratory depression, contraindicated with alcohol and sedative-hypnotics, high sodium load, and misuse potential.

details.labeledFor: Xyrem and Lumryz are FDA-approved for narcolepsy; only Xywav (low-sodium oxybate) is approved for IH.

dosing.start: 4.5 g/night (Xyrem split into two doses; Lumryz once at bedtime)
dosing.notes: Lower-sodium Xywav is preferred in IH; these products carry a large sodium load.

formulations: Xyrem and generic oral solution 500 mg/mL
boxedWarnings: CNS depression: do not use with alcohol or sedative hypnotics
warnings: Respiratory depression and sleep apnea worsening
details.rems: XYWAV and XYREM REMS / LUMRYZ REMS
details.plainSummary: A strong sleep medicine taken at night that can reduce sleep inertia and daytime sleepiness. It is tightly controlled because it can slow breathing and be misused.

references.label: Maski K et al. AASM guideline: treatment of central disorders of hypersomnolence. J Clin Sleep Med 2021
Alkermes: positive topline results from REVITALYZ phase 3 study of Lumryz in IH (2026)

offLabel.use: IH refractory to standard wake-promoting agents
offLabel.notes: Conditional AASM 2021 recommendation based on limited data. Cautions: GI upset, taste disturbance, QT prolongation, strong CYP3A4 inhibition with many interactions, C. difficile risk, and antimicrobial-resistance concerns with long-term use.

details.labeledFor: FDA-approved as an antibiotic; not for idiopathic hypersomnia.

dosing.target: 500 mg twice daily, typically trialed for 2 or more weeks
dosing.notes: Used only when wake-promoting agents fail; review interactions first.

formulations: Tablets 250, 500 mg; ER tablets 500 mg; suspension
contraindications: History of cholestatic jaundice with clarithromycin
Colchicine in renal or hepatic impairment
warnings: C. difficile infection; antimicrobial resistance with long-term use
details.plainSummary: An antibiotic that, in small studies, reduced sleepiness in some people with idiopathic hypersomnia. It affects many other medicines and is used only when other options fail.

references.label: Maski K et al. AASM guideline: treatment of central disorders of hypersomnolence. J Clin Sleep Med 2021
